META’s multiple has fallen to 15X EPS, a 55% PEG discount to peers. We detail why Meta will grow faster for longer and potential agentic catalysts (meet ”MetaClaw”) to drive revisions and re-rating. Macro and regulatory also addressed. META new Top Pick, $775 PT, 50% upside. Sentiment Has Troughed…It's Time to Buy META: META sentiment has troughed due to GenAI ROIC and long-term positioning fears, and more recently macro ad market and regulatory question marks. In all, META now trades at ~15X our '27 $36 EPS, 1 standard deviation below the long-term average, which creates a strong buying opportunity, in our view. Note too that our $36 of '27 EPS 1) Considers some macro weakness (as we reduce ad estimates by 1% in '26 to be more conservative) and 2) Does not factor in the potential $3-7bn of savings from the reported 20% potential workforce reductions (see here)…which all else equal could add $1+ to ’27 EPS (or provide cushion to our base case if ad markets weaken). Our $775 PT has ~50% upside. Exhibit 1: META now trades 1 standard deviation below its 10 year average on our estimates, for only the 4th time in 10 years...which creates a tactical buying opportunity with catalysts ahead...

Source: Company data, Morgan Stanley Research We now turn to addressing the key debates, investor concerns and catalysts to rerate META higher. Debate 1: What is the Monetization Trajectory for Meta's Current Core Products? Our View: We model 28%/21% '26/'27 advertising growth and are 3%/5% above Street '26/'27 revenue. Bottom line, we think the runway is still much longer than appreciated as META continues to improve its organic and paid GPU-enabled machine learning algorithms. We believe engagement (time spent) is accelerating (off of large numbers) which gives META even more time and engagement to monetize, while we believe the time spent growth is high quality and monetizable too given the surge in video-based content. The pipeline is flush also - consider that at 4Q:25 earnings, META talked about 10 improvements yet to come in '26 to drive even more durable engagement and monetization growth in '26 and '27. We discussed this in our '26 TMT conference takeaway note (see here) but we think the company's visibility on forward growth from its core investments remains high (1-2 years)...with one of the next biggest unlocks in '27 likely to be the use of LLMs to analyze META's leading data to further improve its contextual signals. This confidence in more durable core revenue growth helps establish cash flow and EPS floors through META's aggressive investment

Our View: Ship Next Generation Gen-AI Enabled Products to its Leading Corpus of Users. Could a MetaClaw Be In the Cards? As detailed here we believe leading tech platforms' first party data sets with broad distribution are rising in value through the Gen AI/LLM age. This is particularly true for META with 3.5bn+ daily active people across its family of apps, leading and growing engagement (~40/60 minutes spent per user per day on Facebook and Instagram in the US, billions of daily chats/conversations), 250mn businesses and 10m+ advertisers on the platform with robust SKU-level inventory detail and (often) transaction capabilities. And these user and advertiser data sets are only getting stronger (as they grow with improved machine learning, etc) As investors know, META has been investing aggressively in multiple internal foundational models and products for some time. META needs to ship models, but the most important factor we look for is an accelerated pace of next generation product roll outs using LLMs across META’s full user and advertiser bases to further expand consumer and advertiser utility and maintain META’s position at the top of the consumer digital monetization funnel. MetaAI’s future and Meta’s agentic potential remain at the heart of this debate, and as shown below, we think Meta’s platforms combined with a stronger LLM-enabled MetaAI, Manus, and Moltbook creates the potential for a “MetaClaw” agent. Morgan Stanley Research

Morgan Stanley RESEARCH
A prospective MetaClaw could utilize Manus and a stronger Llama LLM as the foundation enabling agentic functionality, and Moltbook as the layer for users personalized agents to communicate with one another. Meta has reportedly (here) been testing the integration of Gmail and Google Calendar into its agent too. Manus already launched an OpenClaw-like product last week that is not yet open source. We look for more innovation ahead but as shown below, META has many natural multi-modal points of communication across its platforms (text, voice, photo) to utilize and create a leading agentic offering for commercial and non commercial behavior.
While they don’t have a browser, 250mn businesses with inventory information and purchase capabilities across Facebook, Messenger, Instagram and Whatsapp create a strong underlying infrastructure to drive agentic shopping. Recall less than 1 month ago Meta already started testing new GenAI enabled agentic shopping (here) and we think there is more ahead. Enabling agentic shopping would drive more durable multi-year “search-like” revenue growth and enable Meta to drive the multi-billion dollar agentic opportunity we detailed in Agentic Shoppers Are Coming… Who Could Win or Lose? (17 Nov 2025).

Morgan Stanley RESEARCH Meta Reportedly Doing a Further Workforce Reduction and the Math: Bottom line, we believe this would be a bullish development and would establish a higher floor on EPS. As detailed in Internet: META: AI Efficiency Winds Starting to Pick Up (15 Mar 2026), we think a potential 20% workforce reduction, if confirmed, could save anywhere from $3-10bn annually. Said another way, we think it could add another $1+ of EPS in ’27. This, in our view, would establish a higher floor ’27 EPS through investment. We don’t think these cuts are in our base model either as we are already modeling heavy investment in D&A and other costs (including hyperscale deals). Source: Company data, Morgan Stanley Research Macro Ad Concerns: We remain highly focused on any weakening of the ad markets due to geopolitical challenges. But a couple key points 1) Advertisers always focus on macro…and so far our latest macro ad checks are more constructive now than a year ago when advertisers were concerned about the pending impact of tariffs. This is not to say that if the MIddle East conflict isn’t resolved and the price of oil doesn't become more manageable the consumer will be immune. Rather (so far at least) we have not picked up on material pull backs in advertising on META in particular. 2) On this point, advertising remains a relative allocation game and META/GOOGL/AMZN would likely be least impacted by pull backs as they have the highest (and rising) ROAS and reach and are performance and transaction driven. More branded and experimental platforms (SNAP/PINS/RDDT/CTV) are likely to see a sooner and larger impact. With all of that said, we have taken a conservative approach and reduced our ad revenue by 1% in '26/'27 this year even as we see 47% upside to shares. Recent Headlines on Content Moderation and Underage Regulation: We are not dismissive of META’s social responsibility to ensure its platforms are safe and not causing negative externalities on society, as we have followed and analyzed Morgan Stanley Research

Morgan Stanley RESEARCH Idea developments around this topic for years. Most recently, news came out last week that Meta faced unfavorable rulings in two separate lawsuits resulting in ~$380mn in total legal penalties. This follows Australia’s recently passed under-16 social media law, France’s imposition of a digital age threshold for social media access, and broader European regulatory momentum around child safety and age verification under the EU Digital Services Act. While we intend to continue to monitor all developments in this area, we highlight three key points that leave us comfortable (for now) that a potential changing regulatory backdrop will be manageable: 1) In a world where we believe the US government is behind and supporting META in order to help make them one of the global AI leaders, we expect to see thoughtful legislation that balances social media access against proposals that could materially impair META. Such cooperation is evidenced by the One Big Beautiful Bill’s impacts (see here) and the addition of META’s CEO to the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology last week as well. 2) We expect any lawsuit, proposals or proposed legislation to take multiple years of appeals and adjustments before final resolution, and 3) Regulation similar to Australia’s would likely result in minimal near-term impact considering the under-16 cohort monetizes at a much lower rate (in some cases 0). As detailed, META needs to continue to deliver upward revisions (to showcase the near-term ROIC) and ship more next generation products. While we don’t know the dates of when new models or products could arrive, we note two potential dates (based on past conference schedules) in May and September. Exhibit 11: We see May and September as potential key catalyst periods for Meta product releases...but are aware it could happen anytime

May 2026?New Models and LlamaCon- What is it? META hosted its inaugural LlamaCon AI developer conference in April 2025. While a 2026 conference has not yet been announced, last year's presentations focused on META's latest products/innovations around its family of models. Media reports have also talked to potential models in May. - Why it Matters? Meta's ability to deliver models and products through these models (MetaClaw?) are important to investors' confidence in ROIC on investment, revenue durability and the multiple they will pay for META
September 2026?Meta Connect- What is it? META typically hosts its annual developer conference in September where the company shares product and technology advances and forward focal points. - Why it Matters? Once again, models, products and pipeline will drive investors' confidence in ROIC, revenue durability and the multiple they will pay for META
